definition: In a biological movement context, an antagonist is a muscle or muscle group that acts in opposition to the main muscle producing an action. The term is often used when describing how agonist–antagonist coordination affects strength and control of movement.

reasons: The packet does not provide a definition of “antagonist” as a muscle/muscle group acting in opposition to an agonist; it only mentions the phrase “agonist–antagonist coordination.”
